LESSON 1
In this lesson we learn the following things:
What is this?
مَا هَذَا ؟
This is a book
هَذَا كِتَابٌ .
Is this a house?
أهَذَا بِيتٌ ؟
Yes, this is a house.
نعم ، هَذَا بَيْتٌ .
No, this is a mosque.
لا ، هَذَا مَسْجِدٌ .
Who is this?
مَنْ هَذَا ؟
#Note:
1. liه is pronounced Iها, but it is written without the first alif
2. Arabic has no word corresponding to the English "is", i.e. Arabic has no copula.
3. There is no word in Arabic corresponding to "a" in English as in "this is a book"
The n-sound at the end of the Arabic noun (kitâbu-n, baitu-n, masjidu-n) is the
Arabic indefinite article corresponding to the English "a"( "an" This n-sound is
called tanwîn.
4. The particle أ placed at the beginning of a statement turns it into a question, e.g
This is a house.
هَذَا بَيْتٌ .
Is this a house?
أهَذا بَيْتٌ ؟

lessons.title: Definite Article and Solar Letters
lessons.focus: Using الْـ, recognizing solar and lunar letters, and reading definite nouns.
notes: The definite article الْـ is like “the”.
With solar letters the ل sound is assimilated in pronunciation.
The first vowel of الْـ is pronounced only when not preceded by another word.

lessons.sourceText:
LESSON 3
In this lesson we learn the use of the Arabic definite article «al» which corresponds to
the English "the" When the definite article «al» is prefixed to a noun naturally the
indefinite article (-n) is dropped, e.g.
بَيْتٌ
البَيْتُ
baitu-n
al-baitu
Arabic has 28 letters. Of these 14 are called Solar Letters, and the other 14 are called
Lunar Letters. In the articulation of the Solar Letters the tip or the blade of the tongue
is involved as in t, n, 1, s, etc. The tip or the blade of the tongue does not play any
part in the articulation of the Lunar Letters as in b, w, m, k, etc.
When «al» is prefixed to a noun beginning with a Solar Letter the «l» of «al» is
assimilated to the Solar Letter, e.g. al-shams (the sun) is pronounced ash-shamsu. No
change takes place in writing ( الشمس). The assimilation is indicated by the
shaddah on the first letter of the noun.
No such assimilation takes place with the Lunar Letters, e.g. al-qamaru (the moon) is
pronounced al-qamaru ( القمَرُ ).
Here are some more examples of the assimilation of the «l» of «al» to the Solar
Letters:
" al-najmu becomes an-najmu
•al-rajulu
becomes ar-rajulu
• al-diku
becomes ad-diku
» al-samaku becomes as-samaku
See the table of Lunar and Solar Letters (page 19 of the Arabic book).
Note that the «a» of «al» is pronounced only when it is not preceded by another word.
If it is preceded by a word it is dropped in pronunciation, though it remains in writing,
e.g. al-bailu. Here the «a» is pronounced, but if it is preceded by «wa» meaning
"and" the «a» is dropped and the phrase is pronounced wa l-baitu not wa al-bailu.
To indicate this omission in pronunciation this sign « e » is placed above the hamzah:
وٱلبَيْتُ
The initial vowel (a, i, or u) which is omitted when preceded by a word is called
hamazatu l-wasl.
The door is open.
The pen is broken.
البَابُ مَفتوْحٌ .
القَلَمُ مَكْسُوْرٌ .

LESSON 8
In this lesson we learn:
1. How to say "this book" in Arabic. We have seen that هذا كتاب means "this is a
book" Now we learn that هذا الكِتابُ means "this book". This is not a sentence.
To make it a sentence we must add a predicate e.g. "this book is new"
. هَذا الْكِتَابُ جَدِيْدٌ
All demonstrative pronouns can be used to make this construction, e.g.
That man is an engineer.

LESSON 9
Part A
In this lesson we learn:
1. The adjective in Arabic. The adjective in Arabic follows the noun it qualifies, i.e.
unlike in English it comes after the noun, e.g.
A new house.

In Arabic the adjective is called na'f (نعتٌ), and the noun it qualifies is called
man'at (منعُوْت) The adjective is in agreement with the noun in the following
matters:
a) Gender. The adjective of a masculine noun is masculine and that of a feminine
noun is feminine, e.g

b) Being definite or indefinite. If the noun is definite the adjective is also definite.

LESSON 13
Part A
In this lesson we learn:
1. The plural of nouns and adjectives. In English adjectives have no plural form. We
say: "good man" and "good men"
But in Arabic even adjectives have plural form.
In English we have two kinds of plural form:
(1) Sound, and
(2) Broken
In the sound plural the word retains its original form e.g
Book → books, pen → pens
In the broken plural the original form of the word is changed to a great extent, e.g.
Man → men, woman → women.
In Arabic we have these two kinds of plural form: sound and broken.

LESSON 16
In this lesson we learn the following:
1. In
Arabic nouns are classified as (1) rational and (2) irrational. They are also
called intelligent and non-intelligent. Rational nouns are those that refer to human
beings. Angels, devils, and such beings are also included in this class. Irrational
nouns refer to things, animals and concepts.
In the singular there is no difference between these two groups. In plural, however,
there is a very important difference. Plural of rational nouns are treated as plural,
so plural words like "they" «these" «those" are used to refer to them. Plural of
irrational nouns are treated as feminine singular, e.g.
Rational (عَاقِلٌ)
Singular:
هَذَا طَالِبٌ جَدِيْدٌ . هُوَ صَغِيْر .
هَؤُلاَءِ طُلَاَبٌ جُدُدٌ . هُمْ صِغَارٌ .
Plural:
Irrational (غَيْرُ عَاقِلٍ)
Singular:
هَذَا كِتَابٌ جَدِيْدٌ . هُوَ صَغِيرٌ .
Plural:
Note:
هَذِهِ كُتُبٌ جَدِيْدةٌ . هِيَ صَغِيْرَةٌ .
So regard the plural of irrational nouns as feminine singular.
1. The students went out.
الطُّلّاَّبُ خَرَجُوا .
2. The dogs went out.
الكِلابُ خَرَجَتْ .
This is the basic rule. There are exceptions to this rule which you will learn later
on.
2. We have learnt some patterns of the broken plural. Here are more:

LESSON 22
We have learnt several groups of nouns and adjectives which do not have tanwîn.
Most nouns and adjectives have tanwîn. Tanwin is omitted in the following cases:
a) When the noun or adjective has ا e.g. كتابٌ : الكِتابُ
b) When it is mudâf, e.g. بلآل
كتاب

C) When it is preceded by يَا c.g. أُسْتَاذُ : يَا أَسْتَاذَ
But there are certain nouns and adjectives which never have tanwîn. They are called
diptotes (in Arabic المَمْنَوْعُ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ).

The Indeclible Nouns
(المبنِي من الأسماءِ)
We have seen that most Arabic nouns are declinable. Some are indeclinable,
ie., they do not indicate their functions by changing their endings. The
following groups are indeclinable (mabni).

1) The ponouns (الضمائو) like :هو، أنتَ، أنا. Likewise tu and huin رأيتهُ (1

LESSON 16
In this lesson we learn the following :
#(1) We have seen in Book Two (Lessons 4 and 10) that most Arabic verbs
are made up of three letters which are called radiclas, e.g., كَتَبَ، جَلَسَ، شَرِب.
A verb consisting of three radicals is called a thuláthi verb (الفِعْلُ الثُّلانِي).
There are, however, certain verbs which consist of four radicals, e.g., ترجم 'he
translated', بسملَ ،he said bismillahirrahmánirrahim, هرْوَلَ ،he walked fast'
A verb consisting of four radicals is called a ruiba'i verb (الفِعْلُ الرَّباعِيُ).
A verb in Arabic may be either mujarrad (الُجَوَّدُ) or mazid (المزيدُ).
a) A mujarrad verb has only three letters if it is thulâthi, and only four letters
if it is ruba'i, and no extra letters have been added to them in order to modify
the meaning, e.g.,

In this lesson we learn the following :
#(1) Kinds of pronouns :
Pronouns are either separate (المُنفَصِلُ) or atlached (المُتْصِلُ).
The separate pronouns are independent and not attached to any other word.
They also occur after yإ, e.g.,

lesson except you.'
The attached pronouns are not independent, but are always attached to other
pronoun meaning 1, and -ka is the attached pronoun meaning you.

grammar.summary: Masculine plural “you”, we, our, and “which”.

grammar.title: أَنْتُنَّ and Time Words
grammar.summary: Feminine plural “you”, كُنَّ, ذَهَبْتُنَّ, قَبْلَ and بَعْدَ.

grammar.title: Rational and Irrational Plurals
grammar.summary: Human plurals vs non-human plurals and feminine singular agreement.

grammar.title: Plural Review
grammar.summary: Continuation of rational and irrational plural agreement.

grammar.title: The Dual
grammar.summary: Two of something, هٰذَانِ, هَاتَانِ, هُمَا, and كَمْ.

grammar.title: Numbers 3-10 with Masculine Nouns
grammar.summary: Counting masculine maʿdūd nouns from three to ten.

grammar.title: Numbers 3-10 with Feminine Nouns
grammar.summary: Counting feminine maʿdūd nouns and feminine one/two.

grammar.title: Review and Test Lesson
grammar.summary: Review with ذَاكَ, colors, نُحِبُّ and country names.

grammar.title: Diptotes
grammar.summary: Nouns and adjectives that do not take tanwin.

grammar.title: Diptotes in the Genitive
grammar.summary: Diptotes take fatḥah instead of kasrah in genitive positions.

grammar.title: إِنَّ, لَعَلَّ, ذُو and Large Numbers
grammar.summary: Emphasis with إِنَّ, hope/fear with لَعَلَّ, possession adjectives, أَمْ, and 100/1000.

grammar.title: Negating Nominal Sentences With لَيْسَ
grammar.summary: لَيْسَ, لَيْسَتْ, لَسْتُ, the bāʾ of emphasis, and ابن.

grammar.title: Comparison, لٰكِنَّ and Numbers 11-20
grammar.summary: The pattern أَفْعَلُ for comparison, لٰكِنَّ, كَأَنَّ, ordinals, and 11-20 with masculine nouns.

grammar.title: The Past Tense and Past Negation
grammar.summary: The māḍī verb, مَا for past negation, نَعَمْ vs بَلَى, and لِأَنَّ.

grammar.title: Subject, Object and Verb Roots
grammar.summary: The verbal sentence, فاعل, مفعول به, accusative objects, hamzat al-wasl, and three radicals.

grammar.title: Feminine Past Forms and أَيُّ
grammar.summary: Second-person feminine māḍī, 11-20 with feminine nouns, أَيُّ, أَظُنُّ أَنَّ, لِمَهْ, and هَاتِ.

grammar.title: Accusative Pronouns and كَانَ
grammar.summary: Past-tense plural forms, object pronouns attached to verbs, كَانَ, ذُو with definiteness, and fractions.

grammar.title: Past Tense Review
grammar.summary: Revision of the māḍī with all non-dual pronouns.

grammar.title: Sound Feminine Plural and Relative Pronouns
grammar.summary: Accusative sound feminine plural, the first-person object pronoun, فِعْلُ التَّعَجُّبِ, vocatives, and plural relative pronouns.

grammar.title: The Present Tense
grammar.summary: Introducing the mudāriʿ, four common verb groups, numbers 21-30 with masculine nouns, and بَيْنَ.

grammar.title: Mudāriʿ Forms, Future سَ and Masdar
grammar.summary: Mudāriʿ isnad, the future particle سَ, negative لَا, masdar pattern فُعُولٌ, and أَمَّا.

grammar.title: More Mudāriʿ Forms and Time Adverbs
grammar.summary: Feminine singular/plural mudāriʿ, نَفْعَلُ, adverbial time, and إنَّ/أنَّ after verbs of saying and thinking.

grammar.title: Mudāriʿ Review
grammar.summary: Full review of the mudāriʿ with all non-dual pronouns.

grammar.title: The Imperative
grammar.summary: Forming the command, hamzat al-wasl, imperative endings, and indefinite mubtada.

grammar.title: Prohibition and كَادَ
grammar.summary: لا الناهية, prohibitive endings, كَادَ, negative لَا with the present, and إِنَّمَا.

grammar.title: يُرِيدُ, Relative مَا and Color Forms
grammar.summary: The verb يُرِيدُ, مَا الموصولة, ذَا, diptote names, feminine colors, بدل, آخَر/أُخْرَى, المصحف, and غير.

grammar.title: أَنْ, Purpose لِـ and يُمْكِنُ
grammar.summary: Mudāriʿ mansūb after أَنْ, لام التعليل, يُمْكِنُ, مُنْذُ, and feminine verb agreement.

grammar.title: Mansūb Endings, كَـ and كُلّ
grammar.summary: Mudāriʿ mansūb endings, كَـ meaning “like”, كُلّ for emphasis, vocative يا أيها, اسم الفعل, and demonstratives with iḍāfah.

grammar.title: Future Negation With لَنْ
grammar.summary: لَنْ with the mudāriʿ mansūb and أَبَدًا for emphatic future negation.

grammar.title: Dual Accusative and Genitive
grammar.summary: Dual nouns in accusative/genitive cases and the patterns أَحَدُهُمَا/إِحْدَاهُمَا.

grammar.title: لَمْ, لَمَّا and Parts of Speech
grammar.summary: لَمْ and لَمَّا with the mudāriʿ majzūm, nouns/verbs/particles, nominal/verbal sentences, مَهْلًا, and neither/nor.

grammar.title: The Three Mudāriʿ Moods
grammar.summary: Revision of the marfūʿ, mansūb and majzūm mudāriʿ.

grammar.title: Sound Masculine Plural and 20-90
grammar.summary: Sound masculine plural iʿrāb, the ʿuqūd numbers, 21-30 with feminine nouns, and لا...ولا.

grammar.title: Numbers Summary
grammar.summary: A full consolidation of number agreement, counted nouns, iʿrāb, hundreds and thousands.

grammar.title: كَانَ, لَا يَزَالُ and Special Noun Cases
grammar.summary: كَانَ with noun khabar, لَا يَزَالُ, case forms of أَب and أَخ, قَبْلُ/بَعْدُ, and selected broken plurals.

grammar.title: Mithāl Verbs and يَجِبُ
grammar.summary: Weak first-radical verbs, diminutives, comparatives, يَجِبُ, and another masdar pattern.

grammar.title: Ajwaf Verbs
grammar.summary: Weak middle-radical verbs in the māḍī, mudāriʿ, majzūm and imperative, oaths, ظَنَّ, يَنْبَغِي, and مَاتَ.

grammar.title: Nāqiṣ Verbs
grammar.summary: Weak final-radical verbs, رأى/يرى, the command أَرِ, and omitted final radicals in majzūm and command forms.

grammar.title: Muḍaʿʿaf Verbs
grammar.summary: Doubled verbs, their māḍī/mudāriʿ/imperative changes, لَمَّا meaning “when”, قَطُّ, أَبَدًا, and polite thanks.

grammar.title: Dual Verb Forms and The Five Verbs
grammar.summary: Dual pronouns with māḍī, mudāriʿ and imperative, dual attached pronouns, and الأفعال الخمسة.

grammar.title: Adjective Agreement
grammar.summary: The naʿt and manʿūt, and agreement in definiteness, case, number and gender.

grammar.title: I'rab of Nouns and Verb Moods
grammar.summary: Declension of nouns, primary and secondary endings, mabni nouns, and the marfu, mansub and majzum moods of the mudari'.

grammar.title: Waw, Extra Min and Wish Meanings
grammar.summary: Uses of waw, لَعَلَّ for hope or fear, the extra مِنْ, لَدَى, and selected plural patterns.

grammar.title: Passive Voice and Na'ib Al-Fa'il
grammar.summary: Passive voice in the madi and mudari', the نائب الفاعل, time adverbs, nisbah adjectives, and collective nouns.

grammar.title: Active and Passive Participles
grammar.summary: Forming اسم الفاعل and اسم المفعول from sound verbs and reading them as descriptive nouns.

grammar.title: Passive Ajwaf Verbs
grammar.summary: Passive forms of hollow verbs such as قَالَ and بَاعَ, and their mudari' forms.

grammar.title: Nouns of Place and Time
grammar.summary: Forming اسم المكان and اسم الزمان on مَفْعَل and مَفْعِل patterns.

grammar.title: Noun of Instrument
grammar.summary: Forming اسم الآلة on patterns such as مِفْعَال, مِفْعَل and مِفْعَلَة.

grammar.title: Ma'rifah and Nakirah
grammar.summary: Definite and indefinite nouns, categories of definite nouns, and how definiteness affects meaning.

grammar.title: Omitting Nun in Idafah
grammar.summary: The dual and sound masculine plural omit their nun when they become mudaf.

grammar.title: Sentence Types and Masdar Mu'awwal
grammar.summary: Nominal and verbal sentences, sentence beginnings, and clauses functioning as masdars.

grammar.title: The Nominal Sentence
grammar.summary: Types of mubtada' and khabar, when the mubtada' can be indefinite, and khabar structures.

grammar.title: Zarf and Maf'ul Fihi
grammar.summary: Adverbs of time and place, mabni zuruf, and words functioning as ظرف.

grammar.title: Lam Al-Amr
grammar.summary: The jussive command for third person and first person plural using لام الأمر.

grammar.title: Idha and Conditional Meaning
grammar.summary: Using إِذَا with conditional meaning and recognizing the jawab al-shart.

grammar.title: Jazim Conditional Particles
grammar.summary: إِنْ and its sisters, two jussive verbs in conditional constructions, and related diminutive review.

grammar.title: Thulathi, Ruba'i and Bab Fa''ala
grammar.summary: Root length, mujarrad and mazid verbs, and the doubled second-radical form فَعَّلَ.

grammar.title: Bab Af'ala
grammar.summary: The form أَفْعَلَ, its mudari', masdar, active/passive participles, and related non-salim forms.

grammar.title: Transitive and Intransitive Verbs
grammar.summary: الفعل المتعدي واللازم, indirect objects, and making verbs transitive through فَعَّلَ or أَفْعَلَ.

grammar.title: Bab Fa'ala and Qad
grammar.summary: The form فَاعَلَ, its masdar, participles, place/time noun, the shifted lam, قَدْ, and ذَوُو.

grammar.title: Bab Tafa''ala
grammar.summary: The form تَفَعَّلَ, its masdar, participles, mutawa'ah, لَمَّا as 'when', and الاختصاص.

grammar.title: Bab Tafa'ala and La of Genus
grammar.summary: The form تَفَاعَلَ, reciprocal meanings, لَيْتَ, and لا النافية للجنس.

grammar.title: Bab Infa'ala and Lawla
grammar.summary: The form اِنْفَعَلَ, mutawa'ah, hamzat al-wasl, and لَوْلَا conditional meaning.

grammar.title: Bab Ifta'ala and Idha of Surprise
grammar.summary: The form اِفْتَعَلَ, assimilation of the extra ت, إِذَا الفجائية, and ظَنَّ with two objects.

grammar.title: Bab If'alla, Ra'a and 'Asa
grammar.summary: The colour/defect form اِفْعَلَّ, رَأَى meaning see or think, عَسَى, and infinitive ما.

grammar.title: Bab Istaf'ala, Kay and Idhan
grammar.summary: The form اِسْتَفْعَلَ, seeking meanings, كَيْ, لِكَيْلَا, إِذَنْ, and negating the madi.

grammar.title: Ruba'i Verbs and Damir Al-Fasl
grammar.summary: Quadriliteral mujarrad/mazid verbs, ضمير الفصل, and the partitive مِنْ.

grammar.title: Separate and Attached Pronouns
grammar.summary: Pronouns of raf', nasb and jarr, separate forms such as إِيَّاكَ, and attached pronoun use.

grammar.title: Maf'ul Mutlaq
grammar.summary: The absolute object, masdar emphasis, number, kind, substitutes for the masdar, and cognate masdars.

grammar.title: Maf'ul Lahu
grammar.summary: The object of reason, masdars of motive, هَلَّا for urging/rebuke, and لا as a conjunction.

grammar.title: Tamyiz
grammar.summary: Tamyiz of quantity and sentence, number review, masdar pattern فُعْل, and the second wonder form.

grammar.title: Hal
grammar.summary: The circumstantial accusative, صاحب الحال, sentence hal, connectors, and agreement.

grammar.title: Istithna'
grammar.summary: Exception with إِلَّا and related tools, connected/disconnected exception, and i'rab of the mustathna.

grammar.title: Nun of Emphasis
grammar.summary: نُون التوكيد الثقيلة والخفيفة with the mudari' and imperative.

grammar.title: Diptotes Review
grammar.summary: ممنوع من الصرف, one-reason and two-reason diptotes, proper nouns, adjectives, and ultimate plural patterns.
